posts.title: Prairie Engine Works: more to tune, weather and a rival feud
posts.body:
The drag setup has a lot more to play with: two-step rpm and launch retard, custom gear ratios, a shift rpm slider, ride height and converter stall. Three saved tunes let you swap setups between passes, and the timing slip shows how each split changed from your last clean pass. The truck pull and the road course get their own new sliders, and the road and pull sheets now suggest a setup change. Hill and pull teams race with your setup.

Road, hill and pull days now have weather, rain included. A rival shop can start a feud with you, trash-talking and copying your build until you beat it in head-to-heads. You can also sell crate engines for side income.

There's a throttle slider next to Start, an announcer calls the drag strip, and real 3D props fill the garage, pull track and pits on Full and Ultra.

posts.title: Scrapline: body styles, weapon bays and a voiced arena
posts.body:
Your robot's chassis now comes in seven body styles, from a plain box to a dome, pancake or invertible. Weapons sit in real bays cut into the body. An open bay is also a weak spot, so a hammer from above can hit your weapon first.

The fight screen is easier to read. The camera follows the action, and each bot gets a card showing its parts, bars and worst damage. An announcer and a commentator call the fights, and there's a crowd, bells and a set of new hit sounds.

There's a home screen with Career and Sandbox modes, plus a daily challenge that's the same for everyone and replay codes you can share. Opponents drive smarter, and flippers now throw bots further in the small classes.

posts.title: Ink: tattoos that look like tattoos, and a calmer needle
posts.body:
Tattoos now look much more like the real thing. Lines are bolder, colour is packed in, and a fresh piece has a pink halo and a wet sheen that fade as it heals. Many motifs (roses, swallows, koi, anchors) have real colour areas now, and leaves and stems are always green. The mannequin has fingers and a face, and the shop's four rooms have their own ambient sound, plus a radio you can switch on.

In the chair, a short wait now comes between touching the skin and the machine starting, so you can aim first. There's a Restart button for a sitting. We also fixed phones stealing your touch mid-line and a crash at the end of a sitting.

Prices, prizes and career gates were tuned too: fewer shop closures and a longer road to your own studio.

posts.title: Lombard: voices, new sounds and more to buy
posts.body:
Customers at Lombard's counter now talk. About half say hello when they walk in, and they react out loud to your offers. A handful of story characters have their own voices.

The shop sounds more alive: the shutter going up and down, the morning paper, a ringing phone, rain on the street, a tram bell and a wax-sealed stamp when you write a pawn.

There are 141 things to appraise now, with a new sports category: skates, a signed puck, boxing gloves and a chess clock. Each has its own 3D model. Pawn tickets, a landscape layout and keyboard shortcuts for desktop are in too.

posts.title: Five new games, new addresses and a studio sting
posts.body:
Five games joined the lineup this week. Lombard is a pawn shop sim on a canal in Mostograd: spot the fakes, haggle and decide how much trouble a good deal is worth. Escapement is a watchmaking career, from a shared repair bench to a manufacture making its own calibres. Scrapline has you design, drive and patch a combat robot. Ink follows a tattoo artist from sweeping floors to running a studio, also in Mostograd. Station Keeper is a space station tycoon where power, air, crew and money all share one network.

The studio now lives at longlight.games, and every game has its own address, like pew.longlight.games for Prairie Engine Works. Games also ask the browser to keep their saves when a phone runs low on space.

Covers and screenshots are twice as sharp on big phones, and version numbers now have four parts, so every small build shows. There's a Sound switch at the bottom of every page too. It's off by default; turn it on and the Longlight sting plays once per visit as the logo's sun rises. The sun moves more now as well: its glow breathes, a low sun wobbles near sunset, and tapping it sends a lens flare across the sky.

posts.title: Prairie Engine Works: more team offers and a steadier garage camera
posts.body:
The Team tab now shows five offers at once, and no two are the same kind of racing. Some teams are shoestring outfits and some are well funded. About half carry a rule, like pump fuel only, iron block, no power adders or an engine size cap. Rules pay a little more, and they go on your race-day checklist.

Anyone who picked Synth or Blend as their engine voice keeps that choice. We also fixed the garage camera: zoomed all the way out, it no longer pokes through the walls or props. The panel now stays at whatever height you drag it to.

On Full and Ultra, cars now have open windows, a cabin and a driver. Belts and pulleys no longer look like they're running backwards at high revs. Ultra also now gets the shadowing and glow it was always meant to have.

posts.title: Prairie Engine Works: race teams and real engine sounds
posts.body:
The career now runs race teams instead of selling engines. Take on team offers, build three engines a season and run series in mud bog, boat drag, truck and tractor pull and hill climb, with Pikes Peak as the finale. Drivers remember you, rival shops build cars for your series, and from 300 rep you can run two teams at once. Watch it replays your team's race in 3D, and the off weeks bring a car show and a sound-off.

Real recordings are now the default engine voice. Rotaries, V4s, singles, twins and inline 5s got their own recordings, plus a new V12 rev and recorded blow-off, backfire and anti-lag bangs.

The garage also got a glass look: floating tab bar, glass panels and popups, swipe between tabs, a live dyno curve on the workshop monitor and a full-screen results card you can share.

posts.title: Frontier Lab: the whole lab is playable
posts.body:
Frontier Lab has grown from a map and a title screen into a full AI-lab tycoon. Raise a seed round, open a sales office in each city, buy compute or build data centers, train and launch your own models (open weights too), win public-sector tenders, and keep an eye on rival labs and the safety regulator.

The last week was audit and polish: pacing, popups and navigation, more incidents, news and tips for the late game, a rescaled rich list and a yearly annual report. It's at version 0.1.61 and still in development.

posts.title: Play here, game pages and a press kit
posts.body:
Three new things on the site this week.

Every game page now has a Play here button. It opens the game right inside the page, over the whole screen, with a Close button on top. The phone's Back button closes it too.

Each game also has its own address now, like game-prairie-engine-works.html. Share one of those in a text or on Discord and the preview shows that game's cover and summary.

And there's a press kit, with our logo, colours, and every game's cover and screenshots, for anyone writing, filming or streaming about our games. It's linked at the bottom of every page.

posts.title: Red Skies 1.5: save codes
posts.body:
Red Skies now has save codes. Back up your campaign as a short code and restore it on another phone or browser. The code is checked before anything is replaced, and nothing is ever sent anywhere.

Save codes first arrived on October 15. Version 1.5 gives them their own number.

posts.title: The Whip joins the lineup
posts.body:
The Whip is a political career game for your phone. You start as a rookie backbench MP in the House of Commons of the made-up Dominion of Caledor and work your way up to Chief Whip, the person who counts the votes and keeps the caucus in line.

It's in development. Every MP remembers what you promised them.

posts.title: Season Ticket hits 1.0
posts.body:
Season Ticket, our soccer club management game, is out as version 1.0. Own a club in the 16-team Kestrel Football League, run the business from your own 3D office, build the squad and the stadium, and change tactics while you watch the match.

It plays a whole career on your phone, even offline.

posts.title: Prairie Engine Works is out
posts.body: Our biggest game so far is released. Put an engine together on the test stand, fire it up and hear it run, then take it to the drag strip or a truck and tractor pull to earn cash and reputation.
